source.title: Belfast Telegraph, 2 June 1967, p. 8 ("Sion tops the poll: rural elections with 96 pc"); Belfast News-Letter, 2 June 1967, p. 2 ("Poll surprises in many areas"); Irish News, 2 June 1967, p. 1 ("96 per cent turned out at Strabane")
source.publisher: Belfast Telegraph (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Contests from the Belfast Telegraph, 2 June 1967, p. 8, checked against the News-Letter and Irish News; unopposed returns from the Ulster Herald, 20 May 1967, p. 14.

note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 1 June 1967. Two divisions were contested, Newtownstewart and Sion, 'the first in the history of the Council' (Ulster Herald, 20 May 1967, p. 14); the other 26 seats were filled unopposed. Doorat, missing from the paper's list of unopposed members, is recorded from the Returning Officer's Notice of Result (Ulster Herald, 10 June 1967, p. 12). Independent gain from Unionist; majority 55; 80 pc poll.
